articles.title: COP31: Ambition goes missing as fossil fuel language drops from draft deal
articles.summary: A cat named Ambition went missing again at COP31 on Thursday. While activists delivered the message with humour, it reflected a serious concern: explicit references to moving away from fossil fuels had disappeared from the latest draft climate agreement. On the eve of the summit's scheduled close, ministers and the…

articles.title: COP31 deadlock persists as countries launch new ‘climate reality check’
articles.summary: With the clock running down at COP31 in Antalya, countries on Wednesday launched a new global check on whether climate promises are being kept, even as ministers remained deadlocked over some of the summit’s toughest questions: who pays, how fast the world moves away from fossil fuels and whether a greener future can…

articles.title: Ukraine: Civilian casualties in 2026 already far exceed previous years’ tolls
articles.summary: This year has seen dramatically higher civilian casualties in Ukraine than any other year since the full-scale invasion of the eastern European country by Russia in February 2022, the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine (HRMMU) said on Tuesday.

articles.title: ‘Peace begins in our hearts’: Children close Muscat forum with a message to the world
articles.summary: Children from across the world sent a message of peace from the Omani capital Muscat on Monday, calling for an end to hatred, respect for diversity and the protection of human rights.

articles.title: First Person: Managing risk on Ukraine’s frontline
articles.summary: Humanitarian workers providing support to communities on the frontline of the war between Ukraine and Russia must balance remaining close to those in need with the heightened risks of operating in a warzone, according to the top UN official in Ukraine.

articles.title: When the rains fail: Preparing for drought in Central America
articles.summary: Across Central America’s so-called Dry Corridor, farming families live at the mercy of the rains. In southwestern Honduras, Anastacio Martínez Gómez has spent most of his 73 years learning to work the land. But experience can only take him so far.

articles.title: ‘Here, you can eat until you’re full’: Oleshky evacuees savour first proper meals in years
articles.summary: In a quiet hospital corridor in Kyiv, staff and volunteers push carts carrying steaming pots of chicken soup, bread and buckwheat porridge to patients recently evacuated from Russian-occupied Oleshky, in Ukraine’s southern Kherson region.
